prompt.context: ChemCo, a U.S.-based manufacturer of chemical products, has come to your firm asking for advice on whether to make an investment. It would like to increase its production capacity for alkaline ash from one million to two million metric tons by 2020, with a total investment cost of $20M. Alkaline ash is a chemical product that is commonly used in construction and electronics manufacturing.
prompt.question: Should ChemCo make the $20M investment to double its alkaline ash production capacity by 2020?

clarifying_info.q: What markets does ChemCo currently sell into?
clarifying_info.a: All necessary information is provided in the exhibits. Ask for the exhibits you need.

clarifying_info.q: What is the breakdown of the $20M investment cost?
clarifying_info.a: The $20M is phased as $5M per year for four years, starting in 2020 when expanded capacity first comes online.

clarifying_info.q: Are there other markets or regions ChemCo could target?
clarifying_info.a: ChemCo has had bad experiences in Latin America before and would prefer not to engage there.

exhibits.title: Alkaline Ash Supply and Demand by Region (Current and 2020 Forecast)
exhibits.shows: A chart comparing current and projected 2020 supply vs. demand for alkaline ash across several global regions: U.S., Europe, China, LatAm, Mideast/Africa, and Rest of Asia. Units are in metric tons.
exhibits.data: Regional breakdown of capacity vs. demand for two time periods (current and 2020 forecast) across six regions: U.S., Europe, China, LatAm, Mideast/Africa, Rest of Asia.

exhibits.title: Expected Cost Change 2015-2020 (U.S. vs. China)
exhibits.shows: A table showing expected percentage changes from 2015 to 2020 in four cost categories (Administration, Raw materials/Energy, Freight, Labour) for U.S. and Chinese producers.
exhibits.data: Administration: U.S. +15%, China +10%; Raw materials/Energy: U.S. -5%, China +15%; Freight: U.S. +20%, China +5%; Labour: U.S. +20%, China +10%.

framework: Market Demand: current and expected demand for alkaline ash in construction, electronics, and other industries across regions
Market Supply: current and expected supply/capacity by region; whether competitors will respond to ChemCo expansion
Incremental Revenues: ChemCo's current and projected market share, price expectations as capacity increases
Incremental Costs: $20M capex, additional fixed costs (e.g., managers), ongoing variable costs at different production levels, opportunity costs

questions.prompt: What does Exhibit 1 tell you about where ChemCo should target its expanded capacity?
questions.guidance: Candidate should compare supply (capacity) vs. demand by region. In the U.S., Europe, and China, capacity already outstrips demand and will continue to do so through 2020 — these are unattractive. LatAm, Mideast/Africa, and Rest of Asia all have demand exceeding capacity. Rest of Asia is especially attractive: demand is expected to grow by ~2 metric tons and capacity is far from meeting that demand. LatAm should be set aside because ChemCo has had bad prior experiences there. Chinese producers, with large surplus capacity and geographic proximity, will be the key competitors for the lucrative Asian market.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2, calculate the 2020 production cost per metric ton for U.S. and Chinese producers. Assume 2015 base costs are: U.S. — Administration $40, Raw materials/Energy $30, Freight $55, Labour $30; China — Administration $50, Raw materials/Energy $110, Freight $40, Labour $25.
questions.guidance: Apply the percentage changes to each cost category for each country and sum to get total 2020 cost. U.S. total should be $176.5/metric ton; China total should be $251/metric ton. The key driver of the U.S. cost advantage is raw materials/energy (U.S. costs fall 5% while China's rise 15%), likely because raw materials are domestically sourced for U.S. producers. Candidate should note U.S. has a significant cost advantage.

math.setup: Apply percentage changes from Exhibit 2 to 2015 base costs for each line item; sum to 2020 total cost per metric ton.
math.answer: U.S. 2020 cost = $176.5/metric ton; China 2020 cost = $251/metric ton

questions.prompt: What is the market price ChemCo can charge, and what profit per metric ton will ChemCo earn?
questions.guidance: Chinese firms, competing for the same Rest of Asia market, will price as low as they can — ignoring fixed costs (administration) and selling at variable cost: $251 - $55 (admin) = $196/metric ton. ChemCo's cost is $176.5/metric ton, so ChemCo earns $196 - $176.5 = $19.5/metric ton. Candidate should note ChemCo is price-competitive even at Chinese floor pricing.

math.setup: Chinese floor price = China total cost minus fixed admin cost. ChemCo profit = Chinese floor price minus ChemCo total cost.
steps: Chinese floor price: 251 - 55 = 196 per metric ton
ChemCo profit per ton: 196 - 176.5 = 19.5 per metric ton
math.answer: Market price = $196/metric ton; ChemCo profit = $19.5/metric ton

questions.prompt: Calculate ChemCo's incremental profit from the capacity expansion in its first full year (2020), and assess whether the investment is attractive.
questions.guidance: Expanded capacity adds 1 million metric tons. Incremental annual profit = 1,000,000 × $19.5 = $19.5M. Annual capex outflow in 2020 is $5M (one tranche of the $5M/year phased investment). Net first-year incremental profit = $19.5M - $5M = $14.5M. The investment pays back quickly and profits grow as demand in Rest of Asia increases. The investment is attractive.

math.setup: Incremental volume = 1M metric tons. Annual profit = volume × profit per ton. Net profit = annual profit minus annual capex tranche.
steps: Annual capex tranche: $20M / 4 years = $5M per year
math.answer: First-year incremental net profit = $14.5M; investment is profitable from day one of expanded capacity

recommendation: ChemCo should make the $20M investment to double alkaline ash production capacity by 2020.
The investment will be profitable in the first year that expanded capacity comes online, generating ~$14.5M net incremental profit, with further upside as demand in Rest of Asia grows.
The U.S. cost structure (particularly lower raw materials/energy costs) gives ChemCo a durable competitive advantage over Chinese producers in the Asian market.
risks: If Chinese producers gain access to cheaper raw materials — through new discoveries or alternate production methods — they will become more price-competitive and compress ChemCo's margin.
An economic downturn affecting demand for electronics or construction would reduce alkaline ash demand in the target Rest of Asia market.
If ChemCo cannot secure buyer relationships in Rest of Asia, the additional capacity may sit idle.
next_steps: Conduct further research on the Rest of Asia market to pinpoint specific demand locations and establish relationships with potential buyers.
Begin construction planning for expanding ChemCo's production facility to meet the 2020 target date.
Monitor Chinese producer cost trends (raw materials sourcing, technology) to track competitive dynamics.
